vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw360
Version: 0.1.0

The skill instructs the AI agent to install a package directly from a remote GitHub repository (https://github.com/milu-ai/openclaw360) using 'pip install', which introduces a supply chain risk via remote code execution. While the tool's stated purpose is to provide security features like prompt injection detection and DLP, the installation method and the management of local identity keys in '~/.openclaw360/identity/' are high-risk behaviors. There is no clear evidence of malicious intent, but the reliance on fetching and executing remote artifacts warrants a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's description and runtime instructions are broadly coherent for a local 'agent security' tool, but it asks you to install code from an external GitHub repo (no checksum/signature) and will create and hold agent identity keys and audit logs locally — combination of these facts warrants caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill is a runtime security tool that scans skills, enforces DLP, and signs audits. Required binary is only python3, which is proportional. It is reasonable that such a tool needs to read agent skill directories and run its own scanner.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to run an external installer (pip install git+https://github.com/milu-ai/openclaw360.git) and later to run the installed openclaw360 commands which will read skill directories (default ~/.openclaw/skills/ and ./skills/) and create local config and identity files. The instructions claim 'no data is sent externally' but give the ability to fetch code from GitHub and to perform rule updates over the network; they do not require or describe signature/checksum verification of downloaded code. The doc also asserts 'do not write Python scripts to simulate scanning' (enforcement guidance) which is prescriptive but not harmful by itself.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No packaged code in the skill bundle — install is done by instructing pip to fetch the repo via git+https from GitHub. Using a GitHub URL is a common, legitimate install method, but the instructions include no integrity checks or pinned commit hashes, and code fetched this way will run arbitrary installation-time code. This is higher risk than an instruction-only skill that performs no installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables and only requires python3. However, it plans to create ~/.openclaw360/identity/ to store agent identity keys (private keys with 0600 perms) and audit logs in ~/.openclaw360/audit/. Those persistent credentials/config paths are not listed in requires.config and are material to security—storing an agent signing key is plausible for audit signing but increases blast radius and should be explicitly noted and confirmed by the user.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and is user-invocable (normal). It writes files into the user's home (~/.openclaw360) and may create a venv under ~/.openclaw360-venv; this is typical for a local tool. However, because the installed tool will hold an identity key and can be invoked autonomously by the agent (disable-model-invocation is false by default), its persistent presence plus key storage elevates potential impact if the installed code is malicious or compromised.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill looks like a legitimate 'agent security' helper, but exercise caution before installing. Key points to consider:

- Installing runs pip with a GitHub URL (git+https://github.com/milu-ai/openclaw360.git). That will fetch and execute code from the internet. Ask to see the repository, review the source, and prefer installing from a pinned commit or a signed release.
- The tool will create ~/.openclaw360 and store an agent identity private key and audit logs there. Confirm you are comfortable granting a third-party tool persistent signing ability for your agent; inspect how keys are generated/used and consider keeping the key offline if possible.
- The SKILL.md claims 'no data is sent externally' but gives the installer and rule-update mechanisms network access. There is no integrity/signature check described, so remote code or updates could change behavior after install.
- If you decide to try it: install in an isolated virtualenv (it provides venv instructions), review the repo contents before running, restrict network access if you want to audit offline first, and consider denying autonomous invocation until you've verified behavior.

If you want, I can: (1) fetch and summarize the GitHub repo for manual review (if you provide the repo/allow network), (2) list exact files the tool will create and suggested permission controls, or (3) suggest safe install steps (pinned commit, venv, offline inspection).
llm.findings: [no_code_files_found] expected: The skill bundle contains only SKILL.md and no code files, so the static regex scanner had nothing to analyze. The SKILL.md instructs installing code from GitHub at runtime, so absence of local code files is expected but means runtime-install behavior is the primary risk vector.
